title: Windowed admission controller & cost-SLA aware scaling for embeddings
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Embeddings ingress experiences unstable p99 latency and high tail for multi-tenant bursts. Existing autoscaler reacts slowly to short-lived surges and queueing causes latency SLO violations and increased unit cost. Goal: Implement a windowed admission controller that admits requests in fixed micro-windows with tenant-level budgets and a cost-SLA aware scaling signal that triggers capacity growth proactively rather than reactively. This ticket covers design, prototype, load testing, and staged rollout.
acceptance_criteria: New admission controller enforces a configurable time-window admission policy per-tenant with soft and hard caps
End-to-end p99 embedding request latency reduced by at least 35% under mixed bursty workload compared to baseline
Autoscaler integrates a cost-SLA signal; when tenant predicted spend exceeds budget and latency risk increases, system recommends instance priority and batch-size adjustments
No significant increase in 50th percentile latency; 95th percentile should improve or remain flat
Canary rollout path with target tenants and automatic rollback on >10% error or >25% p99 regression
Comprehensive dashboards and alerting for admission rejections, window saturation, and cost-SLA overrides
implementation_notes: Admission controller architecture: lightweight token-bucket per fixed micro-window (default 200ms) with tenant-weighted fair admission; implementation in ingress router (go) to minimize serialization latency
Budget model: per-tenant daily token budget + short-window burst allowance. Budget consumption tracked via Redis counter sharded by tenant and window to stay O(1)
Autoscaler signal: combine queue depth, window rejection rate, and spend-velocity to compute a proactive capacity score (0-100). Thresholds tuned from load tests.
Fallback: when budget exhausted, controller emits soft rejections (429 with Retry-After and suggested sampling) and marks low-priority requests for batched background processing where applicable
Operational knobs: window_ms, tenant_weight, soft_cap_ratio, hard_cap_ratio, cost_sla_threshold, proactive_scale_threshold
Performance: admission controller must add <0.6ms median overhead; keep KV operations per request <= 2
design_decisions: Picked fixed micro-windows over dynamic token refill to simplify latency characteristics and make admission behavior deterministic for SLO calculations
Use Redis with local LRU caching for hot-tenant counters to reduce remote calls during bursts; accept eventual consistency for short windows
Soft rejections preferred to hard drops to allow graceful degradation and helpful client guidance (sampling hints) rather than opaque failures
Autoscaler will be advisory at first (recommendation API) and then move to automated scaling after 2 weeks of stable metrics
Batch-size adjustments preferred over immediate instance spin-up for short-lived surges to control cost
comments: 2026-02-26 - Aisha Patel: Kicked off architecture review. Initial sketch favors fixed 200ms windows; raised concern about clock skew affecting per-window counters across nodes.
2026-02-28 - Marco Ruiz: Prototype implemented local windowing with Redis fallthrough. Measured 0.45ms median overhead on p95-microbenchmark.

2026-03-02 - Design review notes: Ops asked for an escape hatch to disable budget enforcement per-tenant via a feature flag. Security requested audit entries for every soft rejection (added to scope).
2026-03-04 - Load testing: Ran mixed-tenant burst tests (50 tenants, poisson arrivals). Baseline p99=1.2s, prototype p99=0.7s, 50th percentile unchanged. CPU on ingress nodes increased 6%.
2026-03-06 - PM review (Elena Morgan): Approved canary plan and recommended 3% of production traffic for initial rollout with top 10 heavy tenants excluded until stability window confirmed.

2026-03-09 - Marco Ruiz: Opened PR #2481 for router changes; tagging reviewers @infra-team @embeddings. Noted trade-off: Redis sharding complexity vs. eventual consistency; chose sharding by tenant hash.
2026-03-11 - QA: Found intermittent 429s for a low-volume tenant due to misconfigured tenant_weight default; fixed and added unit test. Added integration test to simulate cross-node window boundary.
2026-03-12 - Operations (SLA team): Requested two additional alerts: sustained window_rejection_rate > 5% for 5m and cost_sla_score > 80 for 10m. Added to monitoring playbook.
next_steps: Merge PR after final infra review and security audit inclusion
Run extended 24h soak with canary tenants and capture cost delta vs baseline
Execute canary rollout to 3% traffic, monitor p99, error rate, and cost_sla_score
If stable for 48h, iterate autoscaler from advisory -> automated scale actions with ramp controls
Document client-side best practices for handling soft rejections (exponential backoff + suggested sampling header)
Post-rollout: run production A/B experiment for 2 weeks to quantify unit-cost impact and quality regressions, if any
